cited_details.statement: Recommender systems play a pivotal role in delivering personalized recommendations across various domains, from e-commerce to content streaming platforms [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608889].

Recommender systems have emerged as crucial tools to help users navigate vast information landscapes by providing personalized suggestions [https://www.premai.io/blog/large-language-models-for-next-generation-recommendation-systems/].

Traditional models such as collaborative filtering and content-based filtering face significant challenges including a reliance on domain-specific data, limited generalization capabilities, and an inability to provide clear explanations for recommendations [https://www.premai.io/blog/large-language-models-for-next-generation-recommendation-systems/].

Classical recommender systems are effective within clearly defined domains but are limited in adaptability and incapable of providing recommendations for unexplored data [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608889].

The rapid evolution of online services and e-commerce platforms has produced an overwhelming amount of information for users to process [https://www.premai.io/blog/large-language-models-for-next-generation-recommendation-systems/].

Recent advancements in natural language processing have introduced large language models that exhibit remarkable capabilities in understanding and generating human-like text [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608889].
Large language models exhibit contextual awareness and strong adaptability to unseen data [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608889].

Combining traditional recommender systems with large language models creates a powerful tool for delivering contextual and relevant recommendations, even in cold scenarios characterized by high data sparsity [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608889].

Large language models revolutionize recommendation systems by enhancing personalization, explainability, and adaptability [https://www.premai.io/blog/large-language-models-for-next-generation-recommendation-systems/].

Large language models transform recommendation systems by addressing challenges like domain-specific limitations, cold-start issues, and explainability gaps [https://www.premai.io/blog/large-language-models-for-next-generation-recommendation-systems/].

Large language models enable personalized, explainable, and conversational recommendations through zero-shot learning and open-domain knowledge [https://www.premai.io/blog/large-language-models-for-next-generation-recommendation-systems/].

Large language models such as ChatGPT have showcased remarkable abilities in solving general tasks, demonstrating the potential for applications in recommender systems [https://arxiv.org/html/2401.04997v1].
Researchers have proposed a general framework for utilizing large language models in recommendation tasks through prompting engineering [https://arxiv.org/html/2401.04997v1].

The framework formalizes the input of large language models for recommendation into natural language prompts with two key aspects and explains how it can be generalized to various recommender scenarios [https://arxiv.org/html/2401.04997v1].
There has been growing interest in developing next-generation recommender systems based on pretrained large language models [https://doi.org/10.1145/3589334.3645347].

The semantic gap between natural language and recommendation tasks remains not well addressed, leading to issues such as spuriously correlated user and item descriptors, ineffective language modeling on user and item data, and inefficient recommendations via auto-regression [https://doi.org/10.1145/3589334.3645347].

Retrieval-augmented Recommender Systems combine the strengths of retrieval-based and generation-based models to enhance the ability of recommender systems to provide relevant suggestions, particularly in cold scenarios [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608889].

The Retrieval-augmented Recommender Systems approach was introduced to explore the possibilities of integrating large language models into recommender systems [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608889].
RALLRec+ introduces representation learning and reasoning empowered retrieval-augmented large language model recommendation [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0957417425031239].
TALLRec presents an effective and efficient tuning framework to align large language models with recommendation [https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.00447].
CLLM4Rec is the first generative recommender system that tightly integrates the LLM paradigm and ID paradigm of recommender systems [https://doi.org/10.1145/3589334.3645347].
CLLM4Rec extends the vocabulary of pretrained LLMs with user and item ID tokens to faithfully model user and item collaborative and content semantics [https://doi.org/10.1145/3589334.3645347].

CLLM4Rec proposes a novel soft and hard prompting strategy to effectively learn user and item collaborative and content token embeddings via language modeling on recommender-system-specific corpora [https://doi.org/10.1145/3589334.3645347].

Sequential recommender systems aim to predict users' subsequent choices based on their historical interactions and have found applications in diverse fields such as e-commerce and social media [https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/poster/93061].
In real-world systems most users interact with only a handful of items while the majority of items are seldom consumed [https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/poster/93061].
These two issues are known as the long-tail user and long-tail item challenges [https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/poster/93061].
These long-tail challenges often pose difficulties for existing sequential recommender systems [https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/poster/93061].
These long-tail challenges can adversely affect user experience and seller benefits [https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/poster/93061].
Existing sequential recommender systems still struggle with the seesaw or noisy issues due to the intrinsic scarcity of interactions [https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/poster/93061].
Advancements in large language models present a promising solution to long-tail sequential recommendation problems from a semantic perspective [https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/poster/93061].
LLM-ESR is one of the pioneers in using large language models to enhance long-tailed sequential recommendation [https://neurips.cc/virtual/2024/poster/93061].
LLM-RS is a novel framework that leverages large language models to enable explicit reasoning chains in sequential recommendation [https://www.mdpi.com/2227-7390/14/14/2631].
Chat-REC moves toward interactive and explainable LLM-augmented recommender systems by leveraging conversational large language models [https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.14524].

Popularity bias, where popular items are disproportionately recommended and overshadow less popular but potentially relevant items, remains a significant challenge in recommender systems [https://www.amazon.science/publications/large-language-models-as-recommender-systems-a-study-of-popularity-bias].

Recent advancements have seen the integration of general-purpose large language models into the study of popularity bias [https://www.amazon.science/publications/large-language-models-as-recommender-systems-a-study-of-popularity-bias].
